promises.claim: The tour opens the studios and the library for your steps, and the session on the courses sets the first-year fall’s first pieces.
Each rehearsal step rehearses the way you chose to play the scene.
A step trains its skill for up to ${WORK.trainingSteps} steps a piece, and practices the ability it calls on.
In the class it’s due, the preparation is judged and the showing gives its band and its note.
The term’s review counts each piece’s band: once ${ESTIMATE.coursework.shown} or more are due, ${pct(ESTIMATE.coursework.unready)} Unready or not shown is short.
Readiness sets how far each step moves its part, and your condition in class counts in the showing.
Each showing is kept on your record, where Your Work So Far reads your strengths and what keeps holding you back.
Reading the scene to 30% with ${READ.label} opens the questions.
A partner may come to class with another answer to a question you’ve answered, and ask you to keep yours, take theirs or try both.
The showing counts your answers as the table work, and an answer the text doesn’t support can be its note.
An answer that differs from your partner’s leaves the scene together at ${pct(ENSEMBLE.apart)} agreement until you’ve tried both.
On ${SCENE_STUDY.title} and courses like it, Work It Through can name the table work as a problem, with no way to work on it there: an answer the text supports is what fixes it.
A choice pays off once it’s rehearsed, and the rehearsal steps, ${ALONE.label} among them, are what rehearse it, with the rehearsals kept with your partner.
A rehearsal kept with your partner rehearses the choice too, as a rehearsal step does.
The showing counts the choice: what it favors, the abilities it uses, and how far it’s rehearsed.
An aspect left open here can be played its own way in one part of the scene, with Play This Part Another Way.
Every way you choose and show is kept, and Your Work So Far names one you choose most of the time.
A note that’s open and given ${LEARNING.persistent} times, on a part a piece prepares, opens another way to work on it on that piece.
A piece the course revises comes back open, due at its next class, with the note to take.
The band sets how much the class grows the course’s skills, from ${pct(WORK.weight.unready)} of a usual class for Unready to ${pct(WORK.weight.exceptional)} for Exceptional.
The term’s review counts the bands: once ${ESTIMATE.coursework.shown} or more pieces are due, ${pct(ESTIMATE.coursework.unready)} or more Unready or not shown is short.
Under a paired piece, the scene together shows your partner’s preparation, timing, answers and any slip, separately from your band.
Each showing is on your record, and a note still open after ${LEARNING.persistent} times shows in Your Work So Far as one that keeps coming back.
It opens once a note has been given ${LEARNING.persistent} times on the same part and is still open.
${APPROACHES.drill.label} adds a step to the piece, and ${APPROACHES.objective.label} changes what counts most in it.
${APPROACHES.partner.label} works on the part at the next rehearsal kept with your partner.
${APPROACHES.smaller.label} caps the band at Working, and the term’s review counts a Working piece as neither Unready nor Strong.
You can’t ask a partner you haven’t met; Meeting Your Class, or your first class, meets them.
A rehearsal you agree goes on your calendar, and the clock stops at it.
A rehearsal kept moves the piece’s partner part when it’s held, and a request of theirs left open holds the piece’s other steps until you answer.
A rehearsal missed or called off late is held against you until you make amends, and two of them can bring a boundary.
The showing’s scene together shows their preparation, timing, agreement and reliability, separately from your band.
Each scene played together is counted, and Your Work So Far gives how they came out on average from the third on.
A rehearsal booked on a day you’ve called in sick is excused, and costs none of their trust.
A rehearsal kept rehearses the way you chose to play the scene, as a rehearsal step does.
A classmate brings you something once you’ve met them, at Meeting Your Class or in class.
${CHOICES.disagreement[1]!.label} replaces your answer to the question with theirs at once.
An answer can change their trust, which counts when you ask them to rehearse; a boundary asks for a day’s notice.
An evening of running lines kept moves the lines of the scene you share ${pct(CLASS.study.memorization)} of what’s left.
A word after a hard showing lifts your morale ${CLASS.encourage.morale}.
A scene’s lines learned to 30% let you try a way, and a problem in a part of the preparation is fixed by that part’s own step.
The showing judges the scene with each part’s own work and every discovery you kept.
A brief’s take includes its beats’ own work and the ways you kept, as its forecast did.
${ADJUSTMENTS['with-partner'].label} moves the preparation of a classmate reading a brief with you.
A part’s director’s notes are worked on through Work On The Note, by the same ways; Work It Through takes what the notes leave.
Play This Part Another Way works on an aspect the whole leaves open: leave one open to play a part its own way.
Working on an ability’s problem trains it a little, and running into a part trains adaptability.
The profile opens with the guide’s chapter “${CHAPTER}”.
Each ability and technique has its exercise in the Practice column beside it.
A piece of work in School Journey opens into how it was judged.
Your Work So Far, near the profile’s foot, reads the actor your work shows.
Readiness Today shows how ready you are for today’s work, from how you are.
P opens the profile from anywhere but a text box.
Practice is done from the Player Profile, in the row of what it trains.
Each hour of practice moves the clock ${plural(PRACTICE.minutes, 'minute')} and spends its energy.
Every piece of work judged afterward is judged with your abilities and techniques where practice left them.
An exercise counts as experience of the material it names, and a brief built on that material prepares faster.
The material an exercise practices is kept in the record that Material You Know reads.
Stamina has no exercise: a workout under Look After Yourself builds it, and so does a class that trains the body as hard, attended.
A rested hour counts for more: the day’s focus scales every hour, and ${FOCUS.precision.label} most.
Genres is a panel of the Player Profile.
Knowing the genre is part of a take’s preparation: it counts toward the take’s interpretation, and is complete at ${pct(BRIEF.complete.genre)}.
A scene from a play of a kind you know is prepared faster, by the better of Familiarity and Work In It.
A part in a play of a kind you know is learned faster.
Open Its Brief, beside each genre, opens the practice brief written for it.
The genres you’ve worked in are counted in Range.
A brief opens from its genre’s row in Genres, with Open Its Brief.
The take judges each part of the preparation against what completes it, and rehearsal beat by beat.
${BRIEF.steps.rehearse.label} rehearses the way you chose to play it, at ${pct(PLAYING.gainShare)} of the step’s reach.
A classmate reading with you learns it as you rehearse, at ${pct(BRIEF.reader.rehearse)} of the step’s reach.
${BRIEF.steps.read.label} practices imagination and ${BRIEF.steps.lines.label} memory, a little each time the part rises.
Work It Through works one beat at a time: Work It Slowly raises that beat’s own rehearsal.
A new reading keeps ${pct(BRIEF.readingKept)} of the breakdown.
The take uses the reading and the way it’s played: what they lean toward, the abilities they call on, and how far the way is rehearsed.
Each side newly chosen, and each take’s reading, is counted toward the habits Your Work So Far names.
A scene for class is played the same three ways, chosen the same way.
Play This Part Another Way plays one beat its own way, on an axis the whole leaves open.
The take with its reader is what earns a callback; your own result counts nothing the reader brings.
A take with a classmate at ${BAND_LABEL.strong} or better together adds about ${TOGETHER_BOND} to your bond; a slip of theirs you cover at least half of adds ${TOGETHER_COVERED} to their trust.
Run It With Your Partner brings a classmate reading with you ${pct(WORKBOOK.partnerGain)} of the way they have left.
Every take with a reader counts toward Playing With Others, with the slips and those you covered.
A take needs a reading chosen first.
Each take is kept on your work record, and opens there into how it was judged, beat by beat.
A take is practice in the brief’s genres, one session’s worth shared among them.
A take grows ${TECHNIQUE_LABEL.screen}, or ${TECHNIQUE_LABEL.voiceover}, toward where classes level off.
Takes and their readings are read for habits, and a callback answered counts toward Taking Direction.
Work It Through names the problems the forecast shows before you tape: a beat not secure, a turn, stamina late.
Rested, at readiness ${EVALUATION.sufficientReadiness} or more, tiredness costs a take nothing.
Each piece judged is kept in School Journey, the latest ${WORK_KEPT} in full and every one counted.
Your Work So Far reads the record for strengths, and what held each piece back, kept for life, for what keeps coming back.
An ability or technique that held recent work back, with room to grow, is what What To Work On Next recommends practicing.
A showing in class opens the same way from School Journey; the teacher’s note on it is in the scene’s Feedback, under Coursework.
A night on stage is judged in the play’s parts, and the night with the company together is worked out beside your own.
Readiness at the hour is the condition every piece reads.
Patterns are named once ${plural(ARTISTRY.least, 'piece')} of work have been judged.
Where It Would Show Next, beside a brief, suggests the briefs your work so far points to.
Reliability counts the rehearsals with a partner kept, and those you missed.
Taking Direction counts the director’s notes on the craft given, worked and answered, and a note on the weakness your work keeps coming back to says so.
What To Work On Next names the weakness your work keeps coming back to with its count in all, and may put it first.
Only a student in the casting pool is cast, and only one in good standing goes to Yale Rep; ${word(ESTIMATE.missedCallsOut)} missed calls take you out until a term review finds you in good standing.
Being cast puts every rehearsal call on your calendar with its stage, and opens the part’s rehearsal process.
Each call and performance goes on your calendar, and the clock stops at it.
The part’s size and stage set how hard each night is: a lead harder than a featured part, and the Rep harder than the School.
The cast list changes bonds: a classmate in your cast comes ${BONDS.shared} closer, or ${BONDS.leadTaken} less close where a lead went between you.
When the list goes up, your own lead lifts morale ${CAST_LIST.ownLead}, a friend’s ${CAST_LIST.friendLead}, and a rival’s adds ${CAST_LIST.rivalLead} stress.
A Cabaret show is set in a week clear of your casting calls; cast at the School and the Rep at once, you can’t take one.
Only a part you’re cast in, with its run to come, has lines and blocking to learn.
A missed blocking call, or lines under ${pct(PROCESS.offBook)} after the off-book call, is what the next note asks for first.
The lines and the blocking are a night’s preparation, against what keeping every call gives you.
Each call kept or missed counts in the attendance the term’s review counts.
An hour on the part trains memory the first ${word(PROCESS.own.trainsAtMost)} times for each part; an hour with the book does every time.
Work It Through on the part works on a movement’s own blocking, slowly or run into from the one before.
A note comes at a work-through call you come to; one on the lines or the blocking comes first while either is short.
A craft note’s ways are Work It Through’s, and working on one is a try kept in the part’s workbook.
The share of notes taken is part of a night’s preparation, and of Growth From A Night.

Each note on the craft given, worked on and answered counts for life in Taking Direction, with the way you reach for most; a note on the weakness your work keeps coming back to names it, with its count.
Notes still open when the run closes go into your notes from the courses, and the next piece can ask for them.
Working on a note trains adaptability, and a note taken makes that call grow you ${pct(PROCESS.noteTaken - 1)} more.
A choice against the director’s request comes back as a note until the choice changes.
Only a part you’re cast in, with calls to come, can be chosen how to play.
Each call after the read-through rehearses the choice, ${pct(CALL_GAIN)} of what’s left.
A choice against the director’s request is the note at the next work-through.
Each night counts the choice: what it favors, the abilities it uses, and how far it’s rehearsed.
The ways you choose are kept as habits in Your Work So Far.
A scene for class is chosen the same way, on the same three aspects.
The lines and the blocking at what keeping every call gives you, and never under ${pct(NIGHT_LEAST.lines)}, complete a night’s preparation.
A run with ${ESTIMATE.workNights} or more nights by the term’s review is counted: mostly Off is short.
The chair reads what each night delivered at the next casting; a night missed counts as nothing.
Each night is kept in your work, judged movement by movement, with what held it back.
The nights with a company count toward Playing With Others in Your Work So Far.
A night Strong or better, the night together where there’s a company, lifts morale ${ESTIMATE.nights.lift}, an Off one takes ${ESTIMATE.nights.sting}, and nerves add stress before the curtain.
A night grows scene work, feeling, voice and what the play asks, scaled by Growth From A Night, and listening with them.
At the closing, the notes still open go into your notes from the courses for the next piece.
Academic warning keeps you out of the Cabaret and takes you out of a show under way; the summer company takes students in good standing.
A Cabaret week has to miss every casting call and night on call; with the School and the Rep both calling in its weeks, you can’t take one.
Joining puts every evening, call and show on your calendar at once.
Each show has its own rehearsal process, lines, blocking and notes, under its panel.
Each show is a night judged like any other, kept on the run and in your work.
A Cabaret or Summer run counts ${pct(R.weight.cabaret)} of a School production’s in what the chair reads you delivered.
The summer stipend lands in your account each Friday at five, ${usd(SUMMER_CABARET.stipendWeekly)} a week before tax.
The summer stipend is wages on the year’s tax return, with its tax already withheld.
The tour shows you the Haas Arts Library, where every copy is borrowed.
A read trains script analysis and imagination, and research trains script analysis again, each kept in your development history.
Script analysis, which every read trains, is part of the craft a scene’s preparation uses.
